messages.subject: x-axis on every facet and minor tick marks...
parts:
Hey everyone,

 

In earlier exchanges with the group and Hadley Wickham it was established that it is not currently possible to draw x-axis on every facet or minor tick marks on an x-axis of a histogram. However, I really like using ggplot2, so I’ve persisted in my effort to find an alternative solution / “cheat”, i.e. the same visual effect be without a specific R code…

 

I have managed to draw x-axis on every facet with “geom_hline(aes(yintercept= 0))”

 

However, I am unsure of a “cheat” for minor tick marks. Any thoughts would be greatly appreciated!!

 

Thanks!

 

Jonathan

messages.author: 66a7bbbceef834e9
messages.subject: Re: x-axis on every facet and minor tick marks...
parts:
Maybe you could use geom_segment to cheat the ticks. First make a data.frame with the position and height of your ticks:

ticks <- data.frame(x = seq(1, 10, by = 2), xend = seq(1, 10, by = 2), y = 0, yend = 1)

p <- qplot(1:10, 1:10) + 
geom_segment(data = ticks, aes(x = x, y = y, xend = xend, yend = yend)) + 
geom_hline(aes(yintercept= 0))

HTH

Luciano

parts:
Luciano,

 

Thanks for the help!!

 

After fiddling with various options I am close to my desired plots… However, the hundreds of plots are being drawn for a huge dataset after writing a “plot function” (see the script below). Unfortunately the plots only look good under certain scenarios. For example, when creating the data.frame “ticks” if I specify “yend = -1”, it works fine with lots of data (see trial 1, attached). However, with very little data it looks terrible (see trial 2, attached). The only way I can think to get round this is to specify “yend” as a proportion of my largest bin frequency (I hope that makes sense!). Do you know if that’s possible?

 

Also, because I am basically plotting extra data to achieve axis ticks, I have specified “axis.ticks = theme_blank()” or else the plot looks like trial 3 (attached). By doing so, the y-axis ticks disappear. I would prefer this didn’t happen… Is it possible to plot y and x-axis tick marks independently?

 

I really hope you can offer more assistance!

 

Jon

 

 

 

 

ticks <- data.frame(x = seq(0, 475, by = 5), xend = seq(0, 475, by = 5), y = 0, yend = -1)

 

plotfunc <- function(site) {

    ggplot(ALL.EF.DATA[ALL.EF.DATA$Site == site, ], aes(x = Length)) +

    geom_histogram(binwidth = 5) +

    geom_hline(aes(yintercept= 0)) +

    geom_vline(aes(xintercept= 0)) +

    facet_grid(Survey.year ~ .) +

    labs(x = "Length class (5-mm groups)", y = "Frequency") +

    scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0,475), breaks = seq(0, 475, 25), expand = c(0, 0)) +

    scale_y_continuous(expand = c(0, 0)) +
geom_segment(data = ticks, aes(x = x, y = y, xend = xend, yend = yend)) +

opts(axis.ticks = theme_blank(), axis.text.x = theme_text(angle = 90, family = "serif"), axis.text.y = theme_text(family = "serif"), axis.title.x = theme_text(family = "serif"), axis.title.y = theme_text(angle = 90, family = "serif"), panel.background = theme_blank(), panel.grid.minor = theme_blank(), strip.text.y = theme_text(family = "serif"), strip.background = theme_blank(), axis.text.y = theme_text(), axis.text.x = theme_text())

  ggsave(paste(site, ".wmf", sep=""), path = "C:/Bolland/R", width = 6.2, height = 8.7)

}

#make a list of site names

sitelist <- as.list(unique(ALL.EF.DATA$Site))

 

# repeat function for each site, which will render a ggplot and save to your working directory

l_ply(sitelist, .fun = plotfunc)

parts:
Just in case anyone needs to do similar… I have plotted “minor ticks” by plotting breaks as the bin width but only labelling every 5th bin. It isn’t the most elegant script tho!

 

scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0,475), breaks = seq(0, 475, 5), labels=c(0,"","","","",25,"","","","",50,"","","","",75,"","","","",100,"","","","",125,"","","","",150,"","","","",175,"","","","",200,"","","","",225,"","","","",250,"","","","",275,"","","","",300,"","","","",325,"","","","",350,"","","","",375,"","","","",400,"","","","",425,"","","","",450,"","","","",475))

    

Jon
